To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of a single practice in isolation is not effective in teaching and learning science; (2) the use of practices together in an integrated fashion is effective in teaching and in learning science; (3) the use of the practices is not effective in isolation from the core concepts; and (4) the use of all three elements (practices, core concepts, and crosscutting concepts) is effective in teaching science.

(1) students' learning of science is enhanced when they engage in scientific practices; (2) scientific practices can be used in science instruction at all grade levels; (3) students' engagement in scientific practices can be facilitated by teachers who are familiar with these practices and have opportunities to engage in them; and (4) teachers' engagement in scientific and engineering practices can be enhanced by opportunities to engage in these practices in professional development programs. …
